# C1 actor crosshair scanner mode gate

`tools/crosshair_actor_acceptance_proof.py` executes the installed C1 1.1.1.13 scanner entry `439940`, including the original obfuscated code. Only the engine locational trace at `486370` is supplied as a boundary result (entity hit821, fraction0.1); entity821 has actual C1 eType18, actorInfo slot0 team1, viewer team2 and weapon enemy range750. The synthetic memory and trace are identical between runs except the scanner mode string.

Observed primary C1 instructions compare that mode against the actual literal `coop` at `C42378`. `83CC66C` loads the mode byte, `83B0831` loads the literal byte, and `83B0839` compares them. Mode `survival` returns after3953 instructions without reading the actor type. Mode `war` does the same. Mode `coop` reaches actor type read `83C5768`, the original actorInfo resolver `42A670`, team read `845FC2C` and weapon range read `8356F21`, then returns after10284 instructions. All three assertions pass. This demonstrates a real hardcoded client mode restriction before actor classification/range; publishing additional actor team or bounds fields cannot override that string comparison.

This proof does not establish actual live collision traces or prove a complete red crosshair/timer result. The synthetic camera basis is incomplete; the coop case reaches range rejection. The independently retained range proof executes the actual range consumer with supplied distance vectors and proves its distance acceptance and enemy-bit branch. Parent owns client integration and live validation; this worker did not alter C1 code or native gameplay for this finding.

## Shipping client predicate and complete scanner proof

The client integration tree now extends the mode predicate at `8458F2A` (original `test byte[esp+4],al`, followed by original `je82FC061`). The helper reads the actual C1 cgs pointer through `table[global6C3D2B0] XOR3958BEAD`, then category at `+20`; the same primary decode is visible at `43C4A9..43C4C4`. It recognizes only exact Survival, ignoring ASCII case as the existing category policy does. Every other mode executes the exact replaced original test. The true Survival predicate resumes the same existing coop branch: initial actor type/slot checks, visibility checks, actual actorInfo team, weapon range and target/timer publication. The authoritative category string is never modified. Thirteen original bytes covering test plus following branch are guarded before either category patch installs.

`tests/test_survival_crosshair_x86.py` in `Kernel33-integrate-all-20261029` maps the compiled shipping `survival_category.c` fixture and actual C1 scanner entry439940. The only engine boundary double is locational trace. C1 actor positions are populated using the actual inverse of the443D90 encoding (keys073FF35A/EDB436A0/893FEAD3); the real C1 origin decoder and range math execute without substitution. Original Survival returns flags0/target0/timers0; patched Survival returns flags16/target821/settle1000,1000, exactly original coop for identical actor input. Original coop/MP/war/ZM/combat/empty/near-miss results remain unchanged. Friendly and neutral team, outside range, invalid type, corpse type, invalid slot and dead flag cases equal the original coop scanner. The existing zone/install/checksum regression also passes, including mismatch/disabled atomic installation. The DLL builds successfully in both dev and no-console profiles without installation. Real C1 visual validation remains parent-owned.
